result.title: SIRIS: Can LLMs Tell When Simulation Errors Matter in AI-Driven Systems Research
result.summary: LLM agents increasingly drive systems research and rely on simulators to evaluate candidate designs at scale. Simulators are imperfect by design: their modeling limitations can distort predictions yet leave the recommended design correct, or change which design should be selected. We introduce Siris to test whether LLMs can tell these cases apart, judging from their systems understanding when a limitation invalidates the simulator's recommendation. By perturbing a simulator, Siris constructs workload pairs with the same candidates, limitation, and simulator recommendation. The perturbation changes predictions on both workloads, yet a reference simulator supports the recommendation on only one. Evaluating thirteen frontier LLMs on LLM serving design problems, we find that identifying a limitation does not ensure a correct choice, and even the strongest models sometimes abandon valid recommendations. Self-correction through a review turn helps these models restore valid choices but introduces new errors in several others. These findings motivate evaluating systems understanding through design decisions under imperfect simulators.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 Siris：通过扰动模拟器构造候选方案、局限描述与模拟器推荐都相同的工作负载对，只有一侧的推荐仍被参考模拟器支持，以此测试 13 个前沿 LLM 能否判断建模局限是否会推翻推荐，并考察复审式自我修正的效果。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「成对扰动 + 推荐是否仍成立」的诊断范式可能可供核查，用于检验 LVR 中 latent 状态能否区分关键与非关键视觉细节，以及自我修正是否会破坏原本正确的选择。
